ControlsHooks.description: External hooks call your own HTTPS API on gateway traffic. A pre_call hook runs after Quilr's checks and before the model call and can allow, flag or block the request (observe mode logs without enforcing). A post_call hook runs on the final non-streaming response (after Quilr's response checks, before it is cached or returned) and can allow, flag or block it; streaming requests skip it. An on_complete hook exports finished requests in batches. You choose the fields sent, the method, URL, headers, auth and signing, the body shape and how the reply maps to a decision. Secrets are write-only.

info.description:
Configure the Quilr LLM Gateway programmatically: apps, shared providers, quota pools, gateway keys, prompts, budgets and history.

**Authentication.** Tenant administrators enable management for a tenant and issue management keys with the Administration endpoints (verified tenant administrator token). Every other endpoint takes a management key as `Authorization: Bearer qlmgmt_...`. Each operation lists the scopes it requires in `x-scopes`; an empty list on an Administration operation means a verified tenant administrator token.

**Writes.** Updates and deletes of an existing resource require `If-Match` with the quoted `version` (ETag) from the latest read (`428` when missing, `412` when stale). Creates take an `Idempotency-Key`; retrying with the same key replays the original result for 24 hours. Saved configuration reaches the gateway asynchronously.

**Responses.** Every JSON response carries `request_id` (also in `X-Request-ID`) and `Cache-Control: no-store`. Errors use `{"error": {"code", "message", ...}, "request_id"}`. Lists are paginated with `limit` and an opaque `cursor` (`next_cursor` is null on the last page).

**Policy.** General QuilrQL policy authoring is not part of this API. Budget and pricing edits (scope `budgets:policy`) are the only policy-backed writes: each publishes a validated policy revision. When QuilrQL governs a tenant, app settings it governs are saved but take effect only when policy authority is disabled; responses flag them with an `inactive_under_quilrql` warning.

Apps whose names contain `/` or a literal `%` can be addressed with the query-locator aliases under `/app?app_name=...` (marked with `x-alias-of`).

The tenant's individual gateway requests, newest first: app, key, user, requested and served model, provider, outcome, status and error code, latency, tokens, cost, response cache, failover and the guardrail categories and actions. Prompt and response text, detected values and provider error messages are never returned; follow `links.explain` for why one request behaved as it did.

`from` defaults to 24 hours before `to` (or now); the range is at most 31 days. get.description: Requests, outcomes, tokens and cost of every app in the tenant, over all time by default (`from` inclusive, `to` exclusive; a date `to` includes that whole UTC day). Rows are per period (`granularity`: total by default, or UTC month, week starting Monday, day or hour) and optionally per one or two dimensions: app, model, provider, user, key (gateway credential), source or outcome. Filters narrow every number, including totals, and `totals` always equals the sum of every row across all pages. Cost is the cost recorded with each request at request time; requests without one are counted in unpriced_requests instead of being estimated. Request counts exclude the background cache-refresh requests the gateway sends on its own, while tokens and cost include them because the provider bills them. Requests whose user identity was removed by data retention are kept with user null. Periods without traffic are omitted. Credential ids are recorded from 2026-10-16; earlier requests report key null. Grouping or filtering by key reads more data, so prefer a bounded range with it. Results can be up to 60 seconds old. Page with `limit` and `cursor` while the query stays the same; a cursor answers 409 `collection_changed` when the result was recomputed and differs (restart without cursor; a fixed `to` in the past keeps results stable). Rows group by the app's current name while it exists, otherwise the name recorded with its requests, and by the served model. `generated_at` says when the data was read and `data_through` the effective end of the range; `totals.priced_coverage_pct` says how much of the billable traffic has a recorded cost. Queries are limited to {QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS} seconds and 100,000 result rows (422 `result_too_large`). 503 `query_timeout` when the query exceeds its time or read limits (narrow it and retry); 503 `data_unavailable` when the data cannot be read right now. 429 `report_busy` (with a Retry-After header) when too many reports are being computed at once; retry after that many seconds.
